# Using The Repository Harness
<!-- doc-role:overview -->

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

Use the three generated skills as a loop: recover context, keep durable documentation current, then leave a verified handoff.

## Daily Workflow
<!-- doc-role:daily-workflow -->

1. Start or resume with `repo-harness-session-start` and state one coherent feature, blocker, issue, or named objective; an issue need not be a remote-provider issue. It reads repository evidence first, then the newest valid guarded local backup, then scoped Engram when available. It inspects local Git read-only, and claims retain their evidence class.
2. Use `repo-harness-documentation` when durable documentation or visible project state needs updating. Complete the objective's applicable documentation, verification, review, and authorized delivery before closing it.
3. Pause or close with `repo-harness-session-stop`. It verifies evidence and required documentation, writes and reopens one exclusive structured Markdown backup under `.repo-harness/memory-bk/`, then writes Engram when available and reports each outcome independently. Only requested Git work triggers path screening and exact work-unit proposals under repository policy. Start adjacent work in a fresh Pi session through `repo-harness-session-start`.

## Response Preferences
<!-- doc-role:response-preferences -->

To persist your choices, create or edit `.repo-harness/state/preferences/user-preferences.json` by hand, or explicitly ask the agent to save them. The agent never saves preferences on its own. This local file is Git-ignored through `/.repo-harness/state/`. Use a JSON object with at least one of these optional keys:

- `conversationLanguage`: `english` or `espanol`
- `responseStructure`: `standard` or `adhd-friendly`
- `explanationStyle`: `standard` or `plain-language`

Example:

```json
{"conversationLanguage": "espanol", "responseStructure": "adhd-friendly"}
```

`repo-harness-session-start` reads it once at startup through the fixed reader (`harness_tool.py read-preference`). An unknown key or value, duplicate key, or unreadable JSON makes the file invalid. Startup reports a short diagnostic and continues without preferences (standard modes); it never blocks.

For each response axis, an explicit current-session instruction wins, then the file, then `standard`. Modes are never inferred from writing style or behavior. Both modes may combine; they shape replies only and make no clinical claim.

Rule owners: [response contract](../../.repo-harness/rules/response-contract.md), [ADHD-friendly](../../.repo-harness/rules/response-adhd-friendly.md), and [plain-language](../../.repo-harness/rules/response-plain-language.md).

## Integrated Availability
<!-- doc-role:availability -->

The local backup is required in integrated and standalone modes. Integrated mode additionally composes Gentle AI and Engram independently; either can remain useful without the other. Startup checks Engram only after repository and local continuity evidence and checks Gentle AI only at enabled coordination boundaries. Surface failures without claiming missing guarantees. Standalone uses neither external component. Repository owners remain authoritative, and commit, push, and PR remain repository-owned.

## Congruence And Ownership
<!-- doc-role:ownership -->

Run `python3 .repo-harness/check.py` (`python` on Windows) after canonical skills or runtime projections change. Root `.gitattributes` preserves LF checkout bytes through one exact `<path> text eol=lf` rule for every byte-compared generated path, including the checker, manifest, canonical skills and command families, runtime projections, wrappers, and optional exact product projections. Human-owned documents and directive-checked files are outside that generated-path contract. The checker proves on-disk parity, not whether the active process refreshed its registered skill content. Same-process older registered content is an expected cache limitation; defer that optional validation to a fresh process or a supported explicit registry reload without inventing a command. Engram carries temporary cross-session context; repository files remain authoritative.

## Approval Boundaries
<!-- doc-role:approval-boundaries -->

The daily skills inspect read-only by default. Outcomes are `ready`, `paused`, `blocked`, `failed`, `completed`, or `degraded`, and `paused` means human input is actually needed. Explicit safe-sync consent covers bounded fetch plus fast-forward-only integration. Explicit combined commit-and-push consent covers exact staging, commit, checks, one fetch preflight, and one push to the identified upstream. Commit-only and push-only remain narrow. Changed scope, sensitive or unrelated files, divergence, destination or credential changes, destructive integration, hook mutation, or verification failure invalidates consent.

Builder apply is separate and strict only during an explicitly active `repo-harness-builder` skill execution, declared with `--activation builder`: English uses exact `APPROVE` or `DENY`; Spanish uses exact `APROBAR` or `DENEGAR`. The CLI receives the resolved language explicitly and requires both the current plan digest and exact active-domain approval. Under the default `--activation maintenance` the strict domain is absent from the output, `--approval` is rejected, and apply needs only the matching digest. Direct CLI calls default to English. Repository identity, self-hosting, ordinary repository maintenance, generated-file ownership, session skills, and direct questions do not activate this interface. Outside an active builder skill execution, use ordinary conversational approval rules.

A builder run carrying an authority context also prints digests you can review without reading anything private: `authorityContextSha256` for what the approval was about, `targetBindingSha256` for which destination it named, `planSha256` for the changes, and `generationSha256` binding all of them together. Premise values and decision statements appear as explicit redaction markers, and each evidence item appears as a repository-relative locator and a digest. Check that those locators are the files you expect, then approve. If something was wrong the host must refresh the context with a new material revision and preview again, because a corrected answer with an identical plan keeps the same `planSha256` and gets a different `generationSha256`, so the old approval cannot be reused.

## Removing The Harness Manually
<!-- doc-role:manual-removal -->

There is no automatic uninstaller. The help command explains this guide read-only; it never deletes files.

1. Inspect `.repo-harness/manifest.json` and the actual files to list the installed harness skills, commands, and runtime copies. The manifest is an inventory, not permission to delete; preserve modified or unknown content. Inspect any separately installed builder folder too. Do not remove entire `.claude/`, `.opencode/`, or `.pi/` directories.
2. Keep project documentation (README, CHANGELOG, and `docs/`) and useful continuity, preferences, and backups by default. Preserve what you need before removing harness storage.
3. In shared `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore`, and `.gitattributes`, remove only confirmed harness references or rules that are no longer needed. Keep unrelated content, including ignore rules used by other tools. Review other retained documents for links to removed paths and update only those references.
4. Show the exact proposed file deletions and edits, then obtain explicit approval. Remove only the approved harness-specific files; remove `.repo-harness/` last, and only after checking its contents for information to keep. Never delete the repository or other tools' files.
5. Review the diff when Git is available and check for remaining harness entry points and broken links. Start a fresh agent session; an existing session can retain loaded instructions. Do not run the removed checker or reinstall the harness just to verify removal.
